title: Size Selectivity in Heterolanthanide Molecular Complexes with a Ditopic Ligand

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear RE2La2(tta)12(pyterpyNO)2 complex with CN8/CN9 sites

synthesis.procedure: PyterpyNO (0.08 g, 0.25 mmol) and Y(tta)3(dme) (0.21 g, 0.25 mmol) were suspended in toluene (12 mL). After a few minutes a solution formed and was cooled to room temperature. La(tta)3(dme) (0.22 g, 0.25 mmol) was added and the mixture was stirred vigorously for 3 h. Heptane (50 mL) precipitated a colourless solid, which was filtered and dried under vacuum for 8 h (0.35 g, 0.09 mmol, 75.7%). Slow evaporation of a toluene solution gave single crystals of the 6-toluene solvate that collapse with solvent loss on drying.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: sequential room-temperature reaction then heptane precipitation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitate filtered and dried under vacuum; single crystals by slow evaporation of toluene

properties.summary: DC χMT of 5 is 25.13 emu K mol−1 at room temperature, falling to 16.09 emu K mol−1 at 1.8 K, attributed to crystal-field splitting of Dy(III) 6H15/2 and antiferromagnetic Dy–Dy interaction. Linear combination of homometallic Dy2/Dy4 references was used to estimate site occupancy. AC susceptibility (zero and 1 kOe, 10–10^4 Hz) shows magnetization dynamics similar to homometallic Dy4; relaxation times were fitted to Raman plus direct terms.

properties.summary: Millimolar toluene solutions of 6 show only Eu(III) emission when excited at 370 nm. Spectral linear-combination analysis indicates about 65% Eu occupancy of the CN8 site (~30% positional disorder), consistent with NMR; CN9 is more quenched than CN8.

measurements.name: Eu occupancy of CN8 site
measurements.conditions: from linear combination of site emission spectra

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear Eu2Y2(tta)12(pyterpyNO)2 complex with CN8/CN9 sites

synthesis.procedure: PyterpyNO (0.089 g, 0.28 mmol) and Y(tta)3(dme) (0.23 g, 0.28 mmol) were dissolved in toluene (15 mL). After a few minutes Eu(tta)3(dme) (0.25 g, 0.28 mmol) was added and the solution was stirred vigorously for 1 h. Heptane (50 mL) precipitated a colourless solid, which was filtered and dried under vacuum for 8 h (0.44 g, 0.19 mmol, 83.9%). Single crystals were obtained by pentane vapour diffusion into a toluene solution.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: heptane precipitation; crystals by pentane vapour diffusion into toluene

properties.summary: Toluene photoluminescence of 7a is Eu-centred and similar to 7b/7c. Spectral analysis gives ca. 5% Eu occupancy of the CN8 site, showing Y preferentially occupies CN8 regardless of addition order.

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear Eu2Y2(tta)12(pyterpyNO)2 complex with CN8/CN9 sites

synthesis.procedure: PyterpyNO (0.08 g, 0.24 mmol), Eu(tta)3(dme) (0.22 g, 0.24 mmol) and Y(tta)3(dme) (0.20 g, 0.24 mmol) were dissolved together in toluene (40 mL). The light yellow solution was concentrated to 10 mL, heated at 80 °C to dissolve the precipitate, and slowly cooled to room temperature, yielding single crystals (0.25 g, 54.3%). Crystals collapse with solvent loss on vacuum drying.
